<h1 class="profile-name">Elvis Kwame Ofori</h1>

<div class="profile-role">Agricultural, land-use and policy modeller</div>

<p class="profile-lead">I develop economic, spatial, behavioural and computational models to understand how agricultural, land-use, climate and bioenergy policy moves from national objectives to real farms, production systems and places.</p>

<section class="home-section">

<div class="section-heading">
<h2>Research</h2>
<a href="research/">Explore research →</a>
</div>

<p class="home-statement">A national pathway can be technically feasible and still be difficult to implement locally. My work connects aggregate objectives with heterogeneous farms, land resources, production systems and places, asking where adjustment occurs, what it costs, and how policy design changes implementation.</p>

</section>

<div class="featured-project">
<div class="meta">Spatial foresight · Ireland</div>
<h3><a href="projects/goblin-spatial/">GOBLIN-Spatial</a></h3>
<p>Resolving nationally coherent agricultural and land-use transitions across local geography to examine exposure, feasibility and implementation constraints.</p>
</div>

<div class="featured-project">
<div class="meta">Farm-level modelling · Ireland</div>
<h3><a href="projects/ift-biosim/">IFT-BioSim</a></h3>
<p>Bioeconomic microsimulation of heterogeneous opportunity costs, participation, transition support and policy incidence.</p>
</div>

<div class="featured-project">
<div class="meta">Bioenergy · United States</div>
<h3><a href="projects/bioland-us/">BioLand-US</a></h3>
<p>Linking prospective biomass allocation with compatible agricultural land and voluntary contractual access.</p>
